> 泰。小往大來，吉亨。

The eleventh hexagram is usually translated as peace, and the usual picture is calm.

說文 says: 泰，滑也.

滑 in classical Chinese is not "slippery." It is 利 — unimpeded, free-flowing (段注: 滑，利也).

So 泰 is water moving through with no blockage anywhere.

The extension to 通泰, 安泰 follows from that: not the stillness of a pond, which is the most "secure" and least 泰 of all things, but circulation.

## 小往大來

小 is the yin lines; 大 is the yang.

In 泰, 坤 sits above and 乾 below: yin goes outward, yang comes inward.

Which is stated in the judgement as a physical event, not a moral one. The obstructing sort recedes outward; what can unfold goes inward and expands.

## 拔茅茹，以其彙

茅茹: the roots of couch grass, tangled with one another. Wang Bi: 茅之為物，拔其根而相牽引者也 — pull one by the root, and the whole clump comes.

彙 is class, kind. Like pulls like; one root brings the whole bundle.

The 象 makes it a statement about conduct rather than about grass: in a time that is opening, what moves is not one person. It is one kind.

## 包荒 is the sharpest line in the chapter

荒 is not "the distant wilderness" here. Wang Bi: 包荒，包含荒蕪也 — 荒 means the overgrown, the unreclaimed.

So 包荒 is bearing what is rank and unsightly.

Which is a definition of tolerance that has been trimmed of its comfort: not room for what is far away, but room for what is unacceptable at close quarters.

That is what makes 馮河 — crossing a river on foot, without a boat — possible on the same line. Capacities come in pairs: the one who can hold the ugly can also act without a vehicle.

## 无平不陂，无往不复

陂 (bēi): 說文 陂，阪也 — a slope, a tilt, low ground.

No flat ground without a tilt; no going out without a return.

This is placed in the third line, at the top of the inner trigram — the exact moment when the opening looks permanent. The chapter's own correction sits there: the flatness you are standing on is a slope seen from the other direction.

## 翩翩

六四 翩翩，不富以其鄰，不戒以孚.

翩: 說文 翩，疾飛也 — light, flying.

So the fourth line moves easily, does not enrich itself at its neighbors' expense, and does not guard itself with trust.

Three negatives, one posture: the traffic between the two halves of the hexagram has stopped needing to be defended.

## 城復于隍

上六 城復于隍.

說文: 隍，城池也，有水曰池，無水曰隍 — the dry moat outside a wall.

The wall falls back into the ditch it was dug from.

Which is the last word of 泰, and it is not a punishment arriving from outside. It is a description of the material: the wall was always the ditch, rearranged.

## The test

Take something in your life that is currently going well and ask a precise question: is it circulating, or is it still? A still pond feels like 泰 and is the absence of it. The hexagram's own sign of health is that things pass through — including disagreement, including the rank parts.
